source.title: Why ADAM Beats SGD for Attention Models
source.authors: J. Zhang; Sai Praneeth Karimireddy; Andreas Veit; Seungyeon Kim; Sashank J. Reddi; Surinder Kumar; Suvrit Sra

record.file_problem: No file problem noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on BERT and ImageNet. Results differ by task: Adam outperforms momentum SGD on BERT pretraining, while SGD outperforms Adam on ImageNet. This refines the optimizer claim by showing task dependence.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported optimizer outcomes relevant to V4. The paper's ACClip comparisons and gradient-noise measurements do not directly test a listed version; cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out BERT pretraining loss and ResNet50 ImageNet accuracy. These results test V4 in additional settings, although the tuning extends beyond its limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors present heavy-tailed gradient noise as one cause of SGD's poor optimization performance, prove clipping convergence guarantees under corresponding assumptions, and demonstrate ACClip's advantages on BERT tasks. Their ImageNet experiment favors SGD under concentrated noise. The empirical noise comparisons support an explanation rather than establish a universal causal rule about generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares optimizers in attention-model training and ImageNet; it does not reproduce the version's broader set of image-classification and language benchmarks or its limited-tuning protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimizer comparison changes across task and model setting: Adam is favored on BERT pretraining, while SGD is favored on ResNet50 ImageNet training.

fits_no_version.finding: The Transformer-XL experiment on PTB reports training-loss improvements from clipping and adaptivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive methods and clipping can improve optimization speed on attention language models; training loss alone does not establish a held-out performance advantage.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-noise norms appear heavy-tailed for BERT and concentrated for ResNet50 on ImageNet; the paper also proves convergence results under heavy-tailed noise assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-noise structure can help explain optimizer convergence differences. These measurements and bounds do not directly measure any listed generalization effect.

record.peer_reviewed: 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: Optimizer outcomes are reported for a limited set of tasks. The BERT validation-loss comparison is presented in a figure without exact values in the text. No uncertainty is stated for the ImageNet validation accuracies.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows relevant to V4 were left out. ACClip comparisons are comparisons between adaptive methods and do not directly test the version's adaptive-versus-SGD contrast.

untested.parts: Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Held-out performance of convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

The specified learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning protocol; a controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; and a held-out word-level language-model comparison. The study does not establish worse adaptive generalization despite matched or better training performance.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. The reader's verdict directions were inverted: V4 describes an adaptive-method disadvantage. R1/R2 and R3/R4 are paired descriptions of two comparisons, not independent replications. ACClip comparisons were explicitly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
The study does not test language-model benchmarks beyond BERT, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
